How it works

Every engagement follows the same order, whether it is a company or your own next step.

  1. Clarity.

    Define where you are heading and why it matters.

    For a company
    Purpose, ambition, economic logic and priorities.
    For a leader
    What you stand for and what you want next.

  2. Structure.

    Build what makes that direction hold up day to day.

    For a company
    Decision domains, ownership and leadership roles.
    For a leader
    Clear priorities across roles and responsibilities.

  3. Development.

    Turn it into progress that lasts.

    For a company
    A steady rhythm of reviews and KPI-driven decisions.
    For a leader
    Decisions made from clarity, even under pressure.

Start with clarity. The first conversation is free.

What changes in practice.

Sample content. These cases illustrate typical engagements. They will be replaced with real, client-approved case studies.

Strategic AdvisorySample

Founder-led omnichannel retailer

Approx. €35M revenue · 9 months

Challenge
Pricing, hiring and assortment decisions all went through the founder. The leadership team waited.
What changed
Decision domains for five leaders, a monthly strategy review and a weekly KPI forum.
Outcome
The founder moved from daily approvals to one weekly decision review.
Strategic AdvisorySample

D2C e-commerce brand

Approx. €60M revenue · 12 months

Challenge
After fast growth, six departments pursued different priorities and meetings multiplied.
What changed
An explicit North Star, three company priorities and a quarterly review rhythm.
Outcome
One shared priority list, with budget decisions owned by the leadership team.
Executive CoachingSample

Head of Operations, scale-up

New leadership role · 6 months

Challenge
Promoted into a larger role and stuck in constant firefighting.
What changed
A clear role definition, priorities across responsibilities and a weekly planning routine.
Outcome
Leading from priorities instead of reacting to the inbox.

Is this the right fit?

A quick check before you get in touch.

Strategic Advisory fits if

  • Product-market fit is proven.
  • You run an e-commerce or omnichannel company with €20–80M revenue.
  • Growth brings increasing friction.
  • Too many decisions still reach you.

Executive Coaching fits if

  • You are navigating a role change or more responsibility.
  • The routines that got you here no longer hold up.
  • You want to decide from clarity, not pressure.
  • You want direction, with or without a leadership title.

Probably not the right fit if you are still finding product-market fit, need sales or marketing execution, or want hands-on operational support.
